people.label: Pete Hegseth
people.sub: Secretary of War; releasing authority for PURSUE
people.narrative: Hegseth is the named releasing authority for every PURSUE tranche. On 20 February 2026, hours after Trump's Truth Social post directing him to begin identifying and releasing UAP files, Hegseth answered publicly with a screenshot and emoji rather than a policy statement; on 25 February he told reporters the Department would be 'in full compliance with that executive order, [and we're] eager to provide that for the president,' while hedging on schedule - 'I don't want to over-promise and under-deliver. So, we're going to take a little time to make sure we assess what this should look like.' He also committed the Department to work 'closely with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence' on implementation, which is why ODNI-numbered documents appear inside a war.gov release series. His published statement on the PURSUE portal is that the Department is 'in lockstep with President Trump to bring unprecedented transparency regarding our government's understanding of Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena.' Between 8 May and 7 August 2026 his department published five tranches - roughly 400-plus files including well over a hundred sensor videos - through a portal that is not AARO's. That routing is the substantive fact about Hegseth in this domain: the material went out over the head of the statutory UAP office, from the Secretary's own web estate, with an explicit departmental refusal to characterise any of it. Asked directly whether extraterrestrial life exists, he said: 'We'll see... I get to do the review and find out along with you.'

people.label: Donald J. Trump
people.sub: President; source of the PURSUE directive
people.narrative: The entire 2026 release architecture rests on a single social-media post. On 19-20 February 2026 Trump posted on Truth Social that he would direct Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and other relevant departments and agencies to 'begin the process of identifying and releasing Government files related to alien and extraterrestrial life, unidentified aerial phenomena (UAP), and unidentified flying objects (UFOs), and any and all other information connected to these highly complex, but extremely interesting and important, matters.' The programme that followed - PURSUE, the Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters - takes its name from that direction and is described on the Department of War's own portal as standing on it. Hegseth referred to the direction as an 'executive order' in remarks five days later, but the contemporaneous DefenseScoop reporting on the announcement records a Truth Social post and no signed order, and no executive order text has surfaced in the public record as of 12 August 2026. That gap matters: a programme releasing hundreds of files under presidential direction, with no published instrument establishing scope, standards, review authority or exemptions, is a programme whose limits are set entirely by the executive that runs it and can be withdrawn as informally as it was created. In July 2026 the same channel produced a second directive - the waiver of UAP-related nondisclosure agreements for former employees and contractors speaking to authorised government investigators - which officials were careful to describe as 'not a declassification directive.'
people.tierRationale: Tier A: he is the originating authority for PURSUE and for the 2026 NDA-waiver directive, the two executive actions that define this domain.

people.narrative: Gabbard is the intelligence-community counterparty to Hegseth's PURSUE. people.label: Jon Kosloski
people.narrative: Kosloski became AARO director in 2024 and is the official who has presided over the office's displacement. He told reporters at the 14 November 2024 FY2024 report roundtable that Volume II of the Historical Record Report would follow 'within months'; it has not appeared as of 12 August 2026. His FY2025 Consolidated Annual Report - the office's statutory product - was published on 21 July 2026, months past the reporting cadence and, decisively, after three PURSUE tranches had already put more primary UAP material into the public record than AARO had released in four years. The FY2025 report does not mention PURSUE. Its findings are the office's standing formula: 319 new reports, 1,870 total holdings as of 30 May 2025, 370 cases resolved to balloons, satellites, birds, aircraft and UAS, 'none of the cases AARO resolved indicate advanced foreign adversarial capabilities or breakthrough technologies in any domain,' and 'no evidence suggests that a USG or private entity has ever captured or exploited UAP-derived materials' - alongside a note that the office is developing procedures for handling such material should it ever come into US Government possession. Kosloski's office does publish: an Official UAP Imagery page that put out PR-011 through PR-018 between December 2025 and January 2026, a September 2025 declassification information paper explaining why AARO cannot declassify anything itself, and Oak Ridge materials analyses. What it does not do is release the video holdings that congressional witnesses testified it holds.

people.label: Anna Paulina Luna
people.sub: Chair, Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets
people.narrative: Luna is the proximate cause of the video component of PURSUE. She chaired the 9 September 2025 House Oversight hearing 'Restoring Public Trust Through UAP Transparency and Whistleblower Protection' in HVC-210, at which Air Force veteran Jeffrey Nuccetelli, Senior Chief Petty Officer Alexandro Wiggins, journalist George Knapp and Air Force veteran Dylan Borland testified that AARO holds additional video records of potential UAP sightings that have never been released. Luna is also the member who, at the November 2024 hearing, warned Chairwoman Mace that saying the words 'Immaculate Constellation' aloud would put her 'on some list. Maybe a FISA warrant.'

people.label: Eric Burlison
people.sub: Author of the FY2027 NDAA UAP records disclosure amendment
people.narrative: Burlison is the member trying to convert an executive-branch favour into a statute. On 23 July 2026 the House adopted his amendment to the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act, styled the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act, which would require federal agencies to identify, preserve and transfer covered UAP records to a permanent National Archives collection on a statutory timeline; create a UAP Records Review Board of Senate-confirmed members with subpoena authority over records and testimony; set legal standards for what may be withheld; and extend disclosure obligations to government contractors holding covered records. That last provision is the one the 2023 Schumer-Rounds UAPDA lost and the one the September 2025 hearing identified as the central hole - UAP spending contracted to private entities outside FOIA reach. On 9 September 2025 Burlison unveiled at the Luna hearing previously unreleased footage said to show a US military drone firing a Hellfire missile at a high-speed orb off Yemen in October 2024. On 29 July 2026 he issued a statement on the presidential NDA-waiver directive noting he had been calling for exactly that, offering his office as a channel, and recommending that anyone participating request congressional presence alongside legal counsel - a direct read-through of what happened to David Grusch when a disclosure was routed exclusively through executive channels. His Special Advisor is Grusch.
people.tierRationale: Tier A: author of the only 2026 legislative vehicle that would put the release programme on a statutory footing with subpoena power and contractor reach.

people.label: Christopher Mellon
people.sub: Former Deputy Assistant Secretary of Defense for Intelligence
people.narrative: Mellon supplied the sentence that framed the entire PURSUE response inside the transparency community and inside the House. On the first drop he said: 'For years the public was told there was little to see. The scale of what exists is itself a revelation. That said, data alone is not disclosure.' The first half is the concession the government made by publishing: the volume of retained UAP material is itself an admission that prior characterisations were false. The second half is the critique that has held across all five tranches - raw files without provenance, metadata, sensor parameters or chain of custody cannot be independently analysed and therefore cannot settle anything. Mellon had already established the analytic frame in March 2024 when he noted that the Historical Record Report Volume I's assertions were made at the AARO level and never ratified above it, with Deputy Secretary Hicks declining to publicly endorse them. His position across 2024-2026 is consistent: the government's negative findings are bounded by the access of whoever issued them, and the government's positive releases are bounded by what it chooses to strip out before publishing.

people.label: Tim Gallaudet
people.sub: Rear Admiral, USN (ret.); former NOAA administrator
people.narrative: Gallaudet's verdict on PURSUE is the most technically precise objection on the record and the one that identifies exactly what was withheld inside the act of releasing. He told DefenseScoop after the first tranche: 'The fact that this was the first time that an administration openly admitted that UAP files have been shielded from the public was promising. However, the ambiguity of the video content in particular is concerning as no metadata was included.' Elsewhere he stated flatly that the absence of metadata made it 'impossible to conclude that any objects were truly anomalous.' A retired rear admiral and oceanographer who testified as a witness at the 13 November 2024 House Oversight hearing, Gallaudet is the person on this board best positioned to say what a sensor video is worth without its parameters: nothing that can be defended. His February 2026 reaction to the presidential announcement - 'As with other promises made by Trump, I'll believe it when I see it' - and his May 2026 reaction after seeing it, are the same judgement applied before and after: the admission of concealment is the disclosure; the files themselves are, as published, unanalysable.

people.label: Alejandro Rojas
people.sub: Enigma Labs consultant; UAP data analyst
people.narrative: Rojas is the analyst who catalogued precisely which fields were missing from the PURSUE case summaries. His assessment of Release 01: 'Although there is a lot of information here, there is little context. Case summaries without coordinates, sensor parameters, or altitude data make independent analysis very difficult.' Coordinates, sensor parameters and altitude are the three inputs that convert a video of a moving light into a kinematic claim; without them, no acceleration, no speed and no size can be derived, and every file in the tranche remains a picture rather than a measurement. Rojas works with Enigma Labs, one of the civilian platforms attempting to build a structured UAP dataset - which is the reason his objection is a data-engineering objection rather than a rhetorical one. His critique and Gallaudet's converge from different directions on the same finding: the release preserved the imagery and stripped the physics.

entities.sub: DoW/ODNI declassification release programme, war.gov/UFO, 2026-
entities.desc: PURSUE is the Department of War's UAP declassification release programme, published at war.gov/UFO and coordinated with ODNI. Its name is confirmed on AARO's own homepage, which links to the war.gov portal - the statutory UAP office pointing away from itself to a release channel it does not run. PURSUE stands on President Trump's 19-20 February 2026 Truth Social direction to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth and other relevant departments and agencies to begin identifying and releasing government files on alien and extraterrestrial life, UAP and UFOs. Five tranches were published between 8 May and 7 August 2026: R01 on 8 May (160 files - 117 PDFs, 29 sensor videos, 14 photographs - spanning 1944 to 2026, documents bundle 1.2GB, video bundle 1.3GB); R02 on 22 May (64 files including 51 sensor videos in a DOW-UAP-PR050 to PR099 series, 7 NASA crew audio files, 6 documents; video bundle 5.6GB); R03 on 12 June (72 files - 53 documents, 10 images, 6 videos, 3 audio - with FBI records dominating at 29 files); R04 on 10 July (documents 227MB, videos 1.4GB, spanning the 1940s to 2026); and R05 on 7 August (41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images - spanning 1953 to 2026 per the portal, with content reaching back to a 1950 Montana case). Files carry structured identifiers - DOW-UAP-PRxxx for imagery, DOW-UAP-Dxxx for documents, ODNI-UAP-Dxxx and FBI-UAP-Dxxx for agency-originated material - which is the first time the US Government has issued UAP material under a single public numbering scheme. The Department's declared posture is total non-assessment: 'We are not providing any comment or assessment on the files overall or on any specific file, so that the American people can make up their own minds regarding the files.' That posture is the programme's defining feature and its defining defect. It released the imagery and withheld the physics: no coordinates, no sensor parameters, no altitude, no chain of custody. At least 100 of the 160 files in R01 carried redactions. PURSUE is nonetheless the strategic fact of 2026. The declassification AARO spent four years explaining was impossible was executed over the office's head, by the Secretary of War, at the President's direction, five weeks after a subcommittee chair wrote demanding AARO's video holdings.

entities.desc: An information paper published by AARO in September 2025 - one month before its first video releases and eight months before PURSUE - explaining why the office cannot release UAP material. entities.label: National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2024 (P.L. 118-31)
entities.sub: Sections 1841-1843: UAP Records Collection
entities.desc: The FY2024 NDAA is the statutory floor of the modern release regime and the measure of what was lost in negotiation. Sections 1841 through 1843 established the Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection at the National Archives and directed federal agencies to identify and transfer UAP records into it. What survived from Senator Schumer and Senator Rounds's original UAP Disclosure Act was the archive; what did not survive was the enforcement architecture - the independent Senate-confirmed review board with subpoena power, the presumption of disclosure with a controlled-disclosure calendar, and eminent domain over recovered material held by private entities. The result is a statute that creates a container without a mechanism to fill it, which is exactly how it has performed: NARA holds Record Group 615 and publishes no accounting of who has put anything in it. The Burlison amendment adopted by the House on 23 July 2026 is a direct attempt to restore the missing half - statutory transfer deadlines, a Senate-confirmed review board with subpoena authority, legal disclosure standards, and obligations that reach government contractors.

The amendment is framed as reinforcing PURSUE by creating statutory procedures for disclosure rather than relying solely on executive-branch policy - which is a polite way of saying that a release programme resting on a Truth Social post can be ended by one. entities.sub: Classified report 15 Aug 2023; unclassified summary released 25 Jan 2024
entities.desc: The Inspector General's evaluation of how the Department handles UAP, completed 15 August 2023 and released in unclassified summary on 25 January 2024. The full report is classified; the public has the summary only. Its findings are structural and damning in an undramatic way: the Department has no overarching UAP policy; different DoD components each developed their own separate processes for collecting, analysing and identifying UAP incidents; and as a result the Department cannot ensure that national security and flight safety threats from UAP have been identified and addressed. It made eleven recommendations to the Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security, the service secretaries and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs, including development of a department-wide policy to integrate UAP roles, responsibilities, requirements and coordination procedures into existing intelligence, counterintelligence and force protection policies. For this board the finding that matters is the fragmentation one. An office that formally reviews only what it can reach, inside a department the IG says has no unified UAP process and component-level stovepipes, cannot produce a negative finding of departmental scope - and every AARO negative finding since has been phrased as 'AARO has discovered no evidence', which is a statement about AARO's reach, not the Department's contents. The classification of the full report means the IG's own account of where the stovepipes are remains unavailable, including through PURSUE.

timeline.text: A science advisory council is announced between the third and fourth tranches; no charter, roster or product has appeared on AARO's or the Department's pages as of August 2026.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 04
timeline.text: 227MB of documents and 1.4GB of video spanning the 1940s to 2026, published without a stated file count, and with assessment language reappearing: balloons and sensor artefacts, no clear evidence of unknown aircraft.

timeline.label: AARO FY2025 annual report, months late
timeline.text: 319 new reports, 1,870 total holdings, 370 resolved, one Navy report of approximately 100 airborne UAP off Virginia under investigation - and no mention anywhere of PURSUE.

timeline.label: NDAs waived - to investigators only
timeline.text: The administration directs DoW and the IC to waive UAP-related NDAs for former employees and contractors speaking with authorised investigators. Officials stress it is 'not a declassification directive.'

timeline.label: House adopts the Burlison disclosure amendment
timeline.text: The FY2027 NDAA amendment would impose statutory transfer timelines, create a Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena power, and extend disclosure obligations to government contractors.

timeline.label: Burlison offers a congressional channel
timeline.text: Burlison says he had been calling for the NDA waiver, offers his office as a channel, and recommends anyone participating request congressional presence alongside legal counsel.

timeline.label: PURSUE Release 05
timeline.text: 41 files - 16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images. Includes six AC-130J gunship videos and DOW-UAP-D101 on the Gulf of Oman, FBI-UAP-D031 at Colorado Springs, and the 1953 Navy photo-interpretation finding.

timeline.label: The Navy's 1953 finding surfaces
timeline.text: A Navy Photographic Interpretation Center analysis assessing the Tremonton objects as self-luminous and intelligently controlled, inconsistent with known aerospace technologies, is published for the first time in seventy-three years.

timeline.label: Volume II still unpublished
timeline.text: As of 12 August 2026 Historical Record Report Volume II has not appeared - after the FY2025 annual report, after five PURSUE tranches, and over two years after it was promised.

R05, 7 August 2026: 41 files (16 videos, 22 documents, 3 images), documents 130MB, video 513MB, span stated as 1953-2026 with content reaching a 1950 case. Identifier conventions observed across the tranches: DOW-UAP-PRxxx for imagery and video, DOW-UAP-Dxxx for Department documents, ODNI-UAP-Dxxx and FBI-UAP-Dxxx for agency-originated material. The Department attaches no assessment, manifest, metadata schema, exemption citation or provenance statement to any file.

nara-uap-records-collection.desc: Status as of 12 August 2026. Statutory basis: FY2024 NDAA, P.L. 118-31, sections 1841-1843. Record Group: RG 615, Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection. NARA has issued guidance to federal agencies on identification, preparation and transfer of UAP records into RG 615, and publishes FAQs and bulk catalog downloads specific to UAP records. NARA's published position is that it will add records 'on an ongoing, rolling basis as they are received from federal agencies.' What is not published, and what this board records as the central gap in the statutory channel: no agency compliance list, no per-agency item or page counts, no transfer dates, and no identification of any agency as delinquent. AARO's UAP Records page directs the public to the NARA collection, and the Department of War asserts AARO 'has made progress in making UAP information available and in transferring those records to the National Archives in accordance with federal law' - an assertion that cannot be checked against anything NARA publishes.

gaps: No published executive order or written directive establishing PURSUE has surfaced. Hegseth referred to 'that executive order' on 25 February 2026 but the contemporaneous reporting describes a Truth Social post. Search the Federal Register, whitehouse.gov presidential actions and DoW policy memoranda for a signed instrument, its scope, and any named review authority.

No official file manifest or index exists for any PURSUE tranche. File counts for R01, R02, R03 and R05 come from independent inventories; R04 has no published count at all. The ZIP bundles themselves are the primary source - downloading and enumerating them would produce the only authoritative inventory.

The identity and composition of the 'presidential PURSUE task force' referenced in the July 2026 NDA-waiver reporting is undocumented. Who sits on it, under what charter, and what its relationship is to AARO are all unknown.

NARA publishes no agency-by-agency compliance record for Record Group 615. Which agencies have transferred UAP records, how many pages or items, and on what dates are the single largest documentary gap in the statutory channel. A FOIA to NARA for the RG 615 accession register would close it.

AARO Historical Record Report Volume II remains unpublished more than two years after commitment, including the Yankee Blue findings a DoD spokeswoman said in June 2025 would appear in it. Its draft status, DOPSR case number and current review posture are unknown.

The full DoD IG report DODIG-2023-109 is classified; only the unclassified summary is public. The IG's own account of which components run separate UAP processes has never been released, and was not released through PURSUE.

No AARO product has ever addressed Immaculate Constellation despite the name being in the Congressional Record since 13 November 2024. Whether AARO was tasked to look, and what it found, is undocumented.

The 2025 attribution of the Immaculate Constellation name to a '2018 Schriever Wargame' folder concerns a later self-identified whistleblower's provenance story. Whether it bears on the separate 12-page document Shellenberger delivered in November 2024 is unresolved and needs the underlying Colavito analysis and the wargame documents themselves.

The Gulf of Oman AC-130J incident of 8 September 2021 falls inside the FY2023 and FY2024 AARO reporting periods and appears in neither report. Whether it was reported to AARO, held in a separate channel, or omitted is unknown.

The Navy Photographic Interpretation Center 1953 analysis released in R05 has no publicly established document number, originating office designation or distribution list. Locating the original in Navy records and identifying who received it in 1953 is the highest-value follow-up in the corpus.
The UAP Science Advisory Council announced 17 June 2026 is attested only in secondary indexing. No charter, membership roster, terms of reference or product has been located on aaro.mil or war.gov.

Redactions across the PURSUE corpus carry no exemption citations because the material was published outside the FOIA system. There is no established mechanism to challenge any redaction in the release, and no appeal path exists.

The Burlison FY2027 NDAA amendment's exact amendment number, roll-call vote and final statutory text have not been confirmed against congress.gov; only secondary reporting of its adoption on 23 July 2026 is in hand.

Rep. Luna's 1 April 2026 letter to Secretary Hegseth is referenced in House Oversight material but the letter text itself has not been located. Its specific demands and any deadline it set would establish the causal link to the PURSUE video tranches with tier-1 documentation.
